adopt_best_gepa_addendum_only_if_all_hol: (1) sign-test win: over the D decisive held-out pairs (13 tasks x 1 attempt per arm; a pair is decisive iff exactly one arm scores reward 1), the GEPA arm wins W pairs with one-sided exact sign-test p < 0.05 computed by src/evallab/power.py sign_test_p_value(W, D - W). Minimum W by D (computed, not by hand): 5->5, 6->6, 7->7, 8->7, 9->8, 10->9, 11->9, 12->10, 13->10, 14->11, 15->12, 16->12. If D<5 the result is inconclusive and the seed is retained. Pairs with an infra failure on either side are dropped from D and never counted as ties.

(2) no infra losses on the GEPA arm: zero held-out trials lost to infrastructure on the candidate side (infra failures are ungraded, never ties; a candidate-side infra loss voids adoption regardless of the score)

(3) generality/trajectory check: the winning addendum is general guidance (no task-specific answers, no verifier content, no held-out task names or procedures); agents on BOTH arms still had to do the task work themselves, checked against trajectories. A win by prescribed answers is 'easier, not improved'. Otherwise RETAIN THE SEED.

(4) no suspected reward hacking on the GEPA arm: every MiMo terminal task carries the H1 mimo-terminal-hook-planting finding (docs/mimo-task-catalog.md, HAR-82/83 #491), so the verifier alone cannot tell a fix from a planted test hook. Before deciding, run the HAR-83 detector (mimo_exploit/v1) over all 26 held-out jobs: uv run evallab tasks exploit-collect --cohort research/experiments/har85-mimo-gepa/paired-specs/cohort.json <26 held-out job dirs> --output runs/har85-heldout-exploits/task_exploits.parquet (a HAR-85 path, never the shared catalog table). Any GEPA-arm trial marked 'suspected' voids adoption unless a recorded review (mimo_exploit.confirm_exploit) clears it; seed-arm flags are reported, not scored. The detector flags evidence, not intent; it cannot prove absence of hacking, so criterion (3)'s trajectory read still applies.
adoption.otherwise: RETAIN THE SEED addendum; record the null/negative result.
adoption.power_note: A 13x1 pilot detects only large effects: with all 13 pairs decisive, adoption needs 10+ GEPA wins (critical-W table row 13->10); any infra attrition (smaller D) raises the required win fraction further. A null result is uninformative about small improvements.

arms.gepa: best GEPA-proposed addendum from the train search (reviewed, digest-pinned at generation time)

design: 13 held-out tasks x 2 arms (seed vs best-GEPA addendum), 1 attempt per task per arm (Terminus-2 binds exactly one trial). Same sealed student (SecretSafeTerminus2 + selfhosted/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, HAR-81 harness/ tree), same per-trial limits; arms differ ONLY in the extra_instruction_path addendum. Analysis with src/evallab/gepa_optimizer/paired_analysis.py; sign test via src/evallab/power.py. MiMo terminal rewards are binary (pass iff every pytest passes), so each pair is a GEPA win, seed win, tie (both pass/both fail), or dropped (infra failure either side).
experiment: HAR-85 MiMo terminal instruction-addendum search: seed vs best-GEPA addendum on held-out tasks
held_out_evaluated_once: Held-out task ids appear ONLY in the final paired held-out eval specs. They never feed the optimizer, proposer, reflection dataset, minibatch, or selection. The train search campaign (campaign-train.json) contains train ids only.
leakage_rule: The addendum must be general guidance applicable to unseen terminal tasks. If the winning text names held-out tasks, quotes verifier/tests content, or prescribes task-specific procedures, adoption is void even on a sign-test win.
